sections.html:
Missoula is the seat of Missoula County in western Montana, spread along the Clark Fork River where the Bitterroot and Blackfoot rivers meet it. Five mountain ranges converge here, which earned it the nickname hub of five valleys. Elevation is 3,209 feet.

Two peaks, Sentinel and Jumbo, crowd the edge of town, and plenty of streets dead-end at a hillside. Hillside lots raise drainage, access and foundation questions a valley-floor lot never does, and buyers bring them up early. Homes near the university and old downtown tend to be older, on tighter lots. North Reserve Street, where Highway 93 crosses the old Mullan Road with quick access to Interstate 90, has been the main retail district since the late 1990s.

The University of Montana, Missoula County Public Schools, St. Patrick Hospital and Community Medical Center drive local housing demand. Staff, students and renters keep looking for places near campus and the hospitals, and moves in and out of town are common.

Winters are cold and moderately snowy, summers hot and dry. Snow averages 39.5 inches a season, usually falling between October 30 and April 20, and snow cover lasts roughly four months.

An inspector's eye goes straight to the roof. Sagging decking, weak attic ventilation and ice dams all show up fast. The furnace gets scrutiny too: December averages 23.9 degrees, and January 1957 hit minus 33 degrees.

Summer cuts the other way, with about 24 days a year at 90 degrees or higher and a peak of 107 degrees, last reached June 30, 2021. Many older neighborhoods have no air conditioning, and buyers feel it during a July showing.

Rivers matter as well. Near the Clark Fork or the Bitterroot? Look at the county floodplain maps first.

Real property tax in Missoula County is split into a November payment and a May payment, each due by the month's final day. If that day is a weekend or holiday, you get the next business day, except for people who received help from the state revenue department's assistance program.

One invoice covers both halves and arrives in late October or early November, so do not wait for a second bill in the spring. The Treasurer's Office takes payment in person, online or by mail, and mailed checks must be postmarked by the deadline.

StageConsequence
After the due date2% penalty plus interest at a 10% annual rate
Late June or early JulyDelinquent notices go out
First business day of AugustTax lien attaches; $75 lien certificate fee
Late AugustOutside investors may buy the lien

From the day a lien attaches, the owner gets two to three years to pay up before the house itself is in danger.

A tax bill you have not paid will not stop a sale, but it must be settled by the time of closing. Have the title company get a payoff figure, then check it against the county's online lookup. If the two differ, phone the Treasurer's Office before closing day. The balance is subtracted from your proceeds.

Sorting this out before you list keeps closing day calm. Any buyer's title commitment will surface tax items and liens, and they are easier to clear while no clock is running.

sections.h2: How to dispute your property valuation
sections.html:
Your home's value comes from the state rather than the county. Residential property is reappraised on a two-year cycle, and the time to object is when the notice shows up.

Two paths exist. The first is Form AB-26, a Request for Informal Classification and Appraisal Review that goes to the department. The second is a direct appeal to the Missoula County Tax Appeal Board. File either one on the state's tax appeal website. Timing is set by state law: object within 30 days of the date on the notice and the result covers both years of the cycle; object later and it covers only the second year, with June 1 as the limit.

Selling while an appeal is open? Your closing figure stays at the billed amount until a decision comes. Pay what is billed and the title company will prorate it. A lower value may cut a later bill.

Your property record card is public, with building, land and characteristic details posted online. Scan it for wrong square footage or bedroom counts before anything else.

sections.h2: Building permits and work without them
sections.html:
Inside city limits, new one and two unit dwellings need a permit and must follow the International Residential Code. Small projects can be exempt. A free-standing residential deck 30 inches or less above the ground is one example.

Unpermitted work is where sellers get stuck. Inspectors and lenders may want permit records for a finished basement, an addition or a garage conversion. Development Services has a page section devoted to work done without a permit. The Zoning Desk takes email, or calls between 10 am and 2 pm at (406) 552-6625.

Property outside the city falls under Missoula County, which has its own guide at missoulacounty.build. Before any repair, find out which office covers your address.

  • Find the parcel on the county property information system.
  • Ask whether past additions were permitted.

Mountain Line runs 14 bus routes serving Missoula, East Missoula, Bonner, Target Range, Rattlesnake and the airport, with paratransit and four park and ride lots. Missoula Montana Airport, run by the Missoula County Airport Authority, is the largest in western Montana. Passenger rail ended in 1979 when Amtrak dropped the North Coast Hiawatha.

sections.h2: What Missoula sellers usually run into
sections.html:
• Roofs and attics worn by decades of snow load.
  • Older homes near campus with deferred maintenance.
  • Inherited houses that need a probate step before they can transfer.
  • Tax bills split across several districts, including city, county, fire and water.
  • Slope, drainage or floodplain questions that surface late in escrow.

Paying cash can shorten that list since no lender appraisal stands in the way, though price and terms still track the house's condition. Weigh any offer against what a listing would net you.

Order a title commitment early, whatever the sale route, so liens and tax items are known. The Clerk and Recorder keeps deeds, surveys and land books searchable online, which helps you confirm the legal description and any easements on your lot.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html: A thin folder now saves time later. Put in your latest tax invoice, your lender's payoff figure, permit records for any addition or finished basement, and notes on the roof and heating. Inherited house? Ask about probate first, because the deed cannot move until it is done. A quick search of the county's deed and record pages confirms your legal description before a title company asks.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Missoula County?
faqs.a: Each half is due by the end of November and the end of May. If the date is a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies. One bill covers both halves.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for late property tax in Missoula?
faqs.a: Expect a 2% penalty and 10% annual interest. The lien attaches the first business day of August, after which the owner has two to three years to pay.

faqs.q: Who sets my home's value in Missoula?
faqs.a: The state does, on a two-year reappraisal cycle. Disagree? File Form AB-26 for an informal review, or go straight to the county's tax appeal board.

faqs.q: Does a Missoula house need a permit for a deck?
faqs.a: Sometimes not. A free-standing residential deck at 30 inches or less above grade can be exempt, along with other criteria. Attached or taller decks call for a conversation with Development Services.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Missoula house with an unpaid tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing takes the balance out of your proceeds after the title company gets a payoff figure. Settling it before listing means fewer surprises.
